title: Heavy-Entity Over-Interfacing Envy
pattern: A method requires a reference to a heavy, highly-detailed struct (`Employee`) even though it only reads a tiny, specific subset of its variables (`rate` and `has_special_skill`).
why_bad: It violates interface segregation. The `Timesheet` is unnecessarily coupled to the entire `Employee` record (including sensitive details like `ssn` and `address`), making it hard to reuse or test with other billable entities.
detection: A method taking a large struct as an argument but only invoking a very small percentage of its getters/fields.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If the method acts as a pass-through coordinator or persistence mapper.
